I am 71 years old. I started working this land when I was 16, and my father taught me everything before that. Never went to school. This year I will grow chili on my 2.2 mu, same as last year. My son works in a factory in the city, so it is just me and my old woman doing the field work.

I will plant the seeds I saved from last autumn. I picked them from the plants that had the fattest peppers and no sickness. I do not buy those new seeds in shiny bags. My neighbor Zhang tried them two years ago and his crop got some strange rot. I stick to what I know.

For plant food, I will go to Old Wang's shop and buy one 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer and one 50-jin bag of urea. That costs me about 220 yuan. For 2.2 mu, that is all I can spend. I put the compound fertilizer in the ground before I plant, and I scatter the urea twice: once when the white flowers come out, and once when the little peppers start growing. I know some people say I use too much, but I saw what happens when you use too little. The leaves turn yellow and the peppers stay small. A bad harvest means I lose everything. Wasting a handful of fertilizer is just losing a few yuan.

I will till the soil with the small rotary machine my cousin owns. We share it. I do not plow deep, just enough to break the hard crust.

Water comes from my well. I pay for electricity to run the pump, so I do not waste water. I will water four times. First, right after I put the young plants in the ground. Second, when the plants flower. Third, when the fruits are small. Fourth, in the hot days of July when the soil gets hard like a brick. Four times is what I did last year, and it was fine.

Bugs come every year. I watch the leaves. When I see the little green aphids or the black spots, I take the sprayer to Old Wang and he mixes the medicine. I will spray three times this year. If I spray too early, it washes off in the rain. If I spray too late, the bugs eat everything. Three times is right.

I hope to get about 1600 jin per mu. That is 800 kg for each mu. Last year I got a little less because the summer was too dry. This year I pray it is normal.
